newsitem.title: UK: London gold dips briefly at fixing, picks up.
newsitem.headline: London gold dips briefly at fixing, picks up.

text.p: Precious metal prices were narrowly mixed on Thursday afternoon with gold, silver and platinum holding opening levels while palladium lost ground.
Dealers said gold dipped briefly but found sufficient buyers to get ahead of morning levels despite early afternoon selling in New York.
It fixed at $345.00 per ounce against $344.85 earlier. New York's Comex April future was down $0.40 at $347.20.
Earlier dealers had said they expected gold to dip to around $342.00 before picking up enough demand to drive it higher. Later it was indicated at $346.00/$346.50.
"There is still a chance of trying $347.00," one dealer said, adding that early selling in New York had not produced the bounce expected so far.
The most significant changes in the markets were the easier platinum and palladium prices.
Platinum was marked down overnight largely through selling against the higher yen on the Tocom while palladium held Wednesday values relatively well until this afternoon.

Platinum was indicated at $363.10/$364.10 down $3.90 but barely changed from opening levels. Palladium at $131.50/$132.50 was down $2.00 with the majority of that being lost after the afternoon fixing of $132.50.
"Russia and Norilsk are still the big story here," one trader said referring to news denying rumours earlier in the week that the giant Russian producer had suffered production stoppages.
"About $10.00 of the price is Russian-related," another dealer said.
Another reasoned that palladium could retreat to under $120.00 once the Russia-Japan talks over the 1997 export contracts are settled.
Dealers said there was no price impact from an announcement on Wednesday that the U.S. Government would sell small quantities of the metals from its strategic stockpile in March.

One dealer said apart from the quantities involved, another reason for market indifference was that as the material was bought up to 30 years ago, its 99.95 assay might be questionable so it may need re-refining before it could reach the market.
